subject: Transition: annual commitment -> flex usage with accelerator
messages:
From: Ethan DeMarco <ethan@crestline.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal request — convert annual to floating usage + accelerator

Hi Chloe / Monica,

Quick background: our existing contract is an annual commit tied to calendar year. Given a shifting product roadmap and variable usage patterns through Q4, we’d like to explore converting the remaining 9 months of our annual commit into a floating, usage-first model with a staged accelerator (to preserve a committed discount during predictable spikes).

High-level asks:
- Convert remaining credit pool to a flexible consumption bucket that can be consumed across product lines.
- Add a 20% accelerator for first 3 months post-conversion to cover anticipated ramp.
- Keep co-term with our corporate billing cycle (Mar 31).

Are these changes something Redwood can support operationally (billing + reporting) and do you have a recommended playbook for implementation? I can share expected monthly burn cadence if helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call early next week.

Best,
Ethan DeMarco
Head of Infrastructure, Crestline AI

Attachments: forecast_summary_q3_q4.xlsx (referenced)
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Ethan DeMarco <ethan@crestline.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal request — convert annual to floating usage + accelerator

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the context. We can absolutely support a conversion like this; there are a few levers we typically align on to balance economics and operational simplicity. I outlined options below and next steps.

TL;DR: Two recommended paths — (A) Co-term float with staged credits + short accelerator (lower admin overhead), or (B) Hybrid: convert a portion to true usage-first and retain a small committed tranche for priority capacity. Both keep your Mar 31 co-term.

Option A — Float conversion (recommended for predictability)
- Convert remaining annual credits into a pooled floating balance that applies across projects.
- Implement a 3-month accelerator (20% of converted value) as a temporary top-up credit applied automatically during Q4 bursts.
- Billing: prorated invoice to reflect conversion and accelerator, then monthly usage invoices.
- Reporting: per-route token breakdown retained; we’ll surface a co-term reconciliation report monthly.

Option B — Hybrid (recommended if you need guaranteed capacity)
- Convert 60% to floating credits, keep 40% as reserved capacity for low-latency endpoints.
- Accelerator applies only to floating portion. Reserved capacity billed monthly as committed capacity.

Operational notes / blockers
- DocuSign amendment required for the conversion + accelerator.
- Finance will need a revised invoice schedule (we should involve Monica for billing cadence).
- Implementation requires a short runbook to map projects to the floating pool.

Next steps
1) If you can share the forecast (monthly burn), we’ll run a quick model and recommend a split (Option A vs B).
2) If you prefer Option A, I’ll prepare a draft amendment + playbook and loop in Monica for billing terms.
3) Propose 30-min call Mon 9/7 or Tue 9/8 — please share availability.

I attached our Renewal Playbook for conversions to this reply.

—
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachment: Renewal_Playbook_Crestline_v3.pdf
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 06 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal request — proposal math and discount impact

Chloe / Logan — forwarding Ethan’s asks and Chloe’s options. I ran a quick pricing back-of-envelope based on last 12 months burn and a Q4 projected spike. Notes:

- If we convert 100% to float and add a 20% 3-month accelerator, effective price realization drops ~8% vs straight annual (because accelerator is additive).
- Hybrid (60/40) preserves ~85% of ARR and gives customer guaranteed capacity for critical endpoints — our SLA exposure is minimized.
- Suggest we propose a time-limited accelerator that phases from 20% down to 5% across months 1-3 to limit long tail credits. Example: 20% / 10% / 5%.

Questions for Chloe:
- Is Crestline willing to accept a phased accelerator? That preserves the promotional nature and reduces revenue impact.
- Monica — can Finance handle a prorated credit and then transition to monthly usage invoices with a final co-term true-up on Mar 31?

I’ll prepare a quick excel (Proposed_Adder_Ramp.xlsx) with scenario tabs to share on the call.

— Priyom
Principal Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Ethan DeMarco <ethan@crestline.ai>, Sarah Li <sarah.ops@crestline.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal request — convert annual to floating usage + accelerator

Ethan / Sarah — thanks for the call today and for sharing the forecast. Summarizing the agreed path and immediate asks so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed path (hybrid conversion):
- Convert 55% of remaining annual credits to a pooled floating balance effective today.
- Retain 45% as reserved capacity (priority endpoints) through co-term (Mar 31, 2027).
- Implement a phased accelerator on the floating portion: 20% month 1, 10% month 2, 5% month 3. Credits will be automatically applied to invoices.

Operational action items (owners / ETA):
- Chloe: Draft amendment and playbook, share for review by 9/09. (Attachment: Renewal_Playbook_Crestline_v3.pdf)
- Priyom: Share scenario workbook and revenue impact (Proposed_Adder_Ramp.xlsx) by 9/09.
- Monica: Confirm invoicing cadence and co-term true-up flow by 9/10.
- Logan: Coordinate the mapping of project ids into the floating pool with Crestline’s engineering lead.
- Crestline (Ethan / Sarah): Sign the amendment once received; provide formal monthly burn forecast for Oct–Dec.

Docs and links:
- Draft amendment (will be DocuSigned): https://app.docusign.com/crestline-deal-3742
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/3742
- Scenario workbook attached for your review.

If that matches your understanding, we’ll issue the amendment today and route to your legal/finance for signature. Appreciate the collaboration — we’ll aim for a fast cutover to avoid Q4 friction.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_Adder_Ramp.xlsx
